The $32B Treasury “bought back in a month” is real. Treating it as one panic purchase of long-term debt is not.

Two programs got added together.

Aug 11 and Aug 18 were $2B liquidity-support operations in 10–20 year and 20–30 year paper. That $2B cap was the normal long-end size until mid-August.

Aug 20 and Aug 25 were smaller fills in 3–7 year coupons, under a $4B cap.

Treasury did not take the maximum.

Sep 3 and Sep 9 were $12.5B each. Those were cash-management buybacks of very short securities, roughly 1 month to 2 years. That size was already on the August refunding schedule.

Most of the headline is two scheduled front-end cash operations, not a surprise raid on the long bond.

How it works: Treasury uses cash already in the Treasury General Account. Dealers offer older off-the-run notes. Treasury accepts the cheapest acceptable offers in a short reverse auction. Legal authority is ordinary debt-management law. The regular modern program restarted in May 2024 after about two decades of almost none.

This does not pay down the national debt. Buying an old note still has to be financed, usually with bills or other issuance. It is a maturity and liquidity swap.

Relative to a $30T+ market that trades over $1T a day, a $2–6B long-end operation or a $12.5B short-end operation is nothing.

What changed is frequency and the recent lift in long-end caps from $2B toward $4–6B after dealers kept offering many times the window.

The method—published schedule, TGA cash, off-the-run paper—is now standard. The bear framing is not.

OPINION: 401Ks

If you have a 401k and you are not self-directing investments, you are doing yourself a disservice.

How I personally invested from ages 22-37:

Age 22-24: Targeted fund (mistake!)
Age: 25-37: 50% growth, 50% S&P 500 (currently 100% in S&P 500 because the new company’s growth fund is shit)

Target funds are the absolute worst thing you could put your money into. Not only will you pay much higher fees (over a .5% difference or in other words, ~6% of your annual gain of ~8%), you will lag the market. It obviously depends on how close you are to retirement for bond allocations, but managed 401K accounts and targeted funds are not allowed to allocate 0% to bonds.  They also over allocate to bonds to smooth the chart. You don’t want bonds when you are young and far from retirement.

HOW TO GO TO SELF-DIRECTED

A good starting point is to get familiar with the different funds your company offers.

1. Compare how each fund in each category compared to $VTI over different time frames to understand how their holdings move with the market.

2. Read the prospectus of funds that matched or beat $VTI. This will allow you to understand the category and strategy of the fund.

3. Understand the fees of the fund. High fees can eat at your ability to compound. Always favor low fee funds if performance is not materially different.

Below are some broad allocations for different funds categories to help you get started with your own research and personal risk profile:

U.S. Large-Cap Equities
- Allocation: 50-100% of total portfolio.
- Role: Stability and steady baseline growth via broad indexes like the S&P 500
- Look for Large-Cap Growth funds and the S&P 500 fund and spread the allocation across both.

U.S. Small-Cap / Mid-Cap Equities
- Allocation: 0-25% of total portfolio.
- Role: Higher growth potential and market-beat tilt.

International Developed & Emerging Markets
- Allocation: 0-25% of total portfolio.
- Role: Geographic diversification outside the U.S. economy.

***If you need help deciding your risk profile, don’t hesitate to reach out to a financial advisor for a personalized approach.***

I hope this helps and I wish you financial freedom in your future!

And if so, why?

I always see posts talking about how bad inflation is so let’s take a look at the economic benefits of inflation/moderate inflation (~2%)

- Stimulates spending: Expecting higher future prices encourages consumers and businesses to buy now rather than wait. This increases overall demand and drives economic growth.

- Reduces debt burdens: Inflation lowers the real value of money. This allows borrowers (including governments and homeowners) to pay back historical debts with cheaper dollars.

- Prevents deflationary spirals: A small cushion of inflation keeps the economy away from deflation, which causes falling prices, hoarding cash, and severe recessions.

- Lubricates the labor market: It permits "real" wage adjustments. Employers can keep nominal wages flat during tough times instead of resorting to layoffs.

- Lowers real interest rates: It reduces the real cost of borrowing, which incentivizes businesses to invest in new projects and expansion.

ASST (Strive) is a Bitcoin treasury company whose value is driven primarily by BTC holdings per share, issuance of common + SATA preferred stock to buy more BTC, and the premium (mNAV) the market assigns to that strategy. Current snapshot (late September 2026): ~26,355 BTC, BTC ~$86,400, common shares ~97 million effective / ~100 million fully diluted, SATA preferred ~$1.12B notional, cash ~$230M, stock ~$29–30, market cap ~$2.8B, mNAV ~1.19×. https://t.co/gWDNsmzAPK
BTC at $250k is a ~2.9× move from here. ASST will not move exactly 1:1 because of ongoing accumulation, dilution, preferred claims, the small asset-management business, and changing premiums.
Conservative estimate: $70–110
Assumptions:
•  Holdings grow only modestly to ~32,000–38,000 BTC (accumulation slows as they get larger and markets tighten).
•  Common shares rise to ~140–160 million from continued ATM issuance.
•  SATA preferred grows to ~$1.8–2.2B (they keep using it as the main funding tool).
•  Net NAV after preferred/cash settles around $4.5–6B.
•  Market applies a compressed 1.3–1.6× multiple on net assets (premium shrinks as the company matures and BTC is less “scarce” on the balance sheet).
This produces a stock price in the $70–110 range. It assumes they still add BTC per share but dilution and a lower premium offset a large part of the BTC price gain.
Bullish estimate: $180–350+
Assumptions:
•  Aggressive continued buying takes holdings to 50,000–70,000+ BTC (they have shown they can add thousands of BTC per quarter when conditions allow).
•  They fund more via SATA and less via common, so shares only grow to ~110–130 million.
•  Preferred rises to $2.5–3.5B but BTC coverage stays comfortable.
•  Net assets for common shareholders reach $10–15B+.
•  Market assigns a 2.0–2.8× multiple (similar to periods when MSTR has traded at a high premium during strong BTC bull markets).
This produces $180–350, with the high end requiring both large additional BTC accumulation and a sustained premium.
Key variables that will decide which side it lands on
•  Pace of BTC purchases vs. share issuance (their “BTC yield” metric).
•  How much of the capital raise stays in SATA vs. common equity.
•  Whether the mNAV premium expands (bull market + execution) or compresses (larger size, more competition from other treasury companies).
•  Operating performance of the asset-management arm and any other assets.
•  Broader Bitcoin treasury sentiment and interest rates (which affect preferred demand).
These are scenario estimates, not predictions. Strive’s own filings and 8-Ks are the best source for updated holdings, share count, and SATA outstanding as 2028 approaches. Treasury stocks can move far more (or less) than the underlying BTC depending on dilution and multiple expansion/contraction.

The historical chart is ugly, but $ASST is a totally different company today than when it first went public.

$ASST originally listed in February 2023 as Asset Entities Inc., a small Discord- and social-media company. It ran Gen Z investment-education servers, influencer marketing, and Discord design/management services. Revenue was modest, losses continued. A failing business.

In May 2025 it agreed to merge with Strive Enterprises, the asset manager co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy. The reverse merger closed September 12, 2025. Asset Entities was renamed Strive, Inc.; the ticker stayed ASST. Strive shareholders took control. Matthew Cole became CEO. The company raised ~$750 million via PIPE (plus warrant potential) and adopted a Bitcoin-treasury strategy: accumulate BTC, grow BTC per share, and try to beat Bitcoin as the hurdle rate while keeping the asset-management business.

In September 2025 it announced an all-stock deal for Semler Scientific, another Bitcoin-treasury company with a medical-diagnostics unit. That closed January 2026, adding thousands of BTC (combined holdings later reported in the 12,000–14,500+ range) plus the diagnostics operations.

The firm is now a Bitcoin treasury plus asset manager, with leftover Discord/social operations. Share count exploded through the merger, PIPE, and acquisition. Market cap is in the billions, but reported losses are large and the stock is highly volatile. Same ticker; fundamentally different company.
